issues.line_text: I'd studied his photos for so long I could draw his face from memoryΓÇöthe line of his jaw, the way his copper hair fell across his forehead, the exact shade of his blue-green eyes. Months of research, of preparation, of waiting for the right moment.
issues.description: Eleanor refers to 'months of research' which reveals investigator behavior too early. According to Story Bible, she's been at Thornewood 6 months (since ~April 2024) but her investigation started earlier. The phrase 'months of research, of preparation' makes her sound like an investigator rather than a predator.
issues.fix: I'd studied his photos for so long I could draw his face from memoryΓÇöthe line of his jaw, the way his copper hair fell across his forehead, the exact shade of his blue-green eyes. Months of waiting, of imagining this moment.
issues.rationale: Removes 'research' and 'preparation' (investigator language) while keeping the obsessive studying behavior (predatory). 'Months of waiting, of imagining' maintains the ominous tone without revealing her investigator role.

issues.line_text: My stomach twisted. Anticipation. Hunger. Something darker I didn't want to name.
issues.description: The phrase 'something darker I didn't want to name' is ambiguous but could read as reluctance about violence (predator interpretation) OR reluctance about her investigation/grief (which would be a spoiler). The diagnostic tests: Does this make her seem like she wants to hurt him? BorderlineΓÇöcould be improved.
issues.fix: My stomach twisted. Anticipation. Hunger. The need to finish what I started.
issues.rationale: More direct and predatory. 'Finish what I started' sounds ominous (readers think: her killing plan) but is actually true (finishing her investigation). Removes ambiguity that could leak grief/investigation motive.

issues.line_text: The friendly exterior didn't fool me. Nobody came to a place like this without reason. Without something to hide.
issues.description: This is investigator thinkingΓÇö'the friendly exterior didn't fool me' implies she's analyzing him skeptically, looking for deception. A predator wouldn't be skeptical of their prey's friendliness; they'd exploit it. This fails the Motive Test (sounds like she wants answers, not to harm).
issues.fix: The friendly exterior was perfect. Made him easy to read. Easy to predict. Nobody came to a place like this without something broken inside.
issues.rationale: Predators see friendliness as vulnerability/opportunity, not as a facade to see through. 'Easy to read, easy to predict' shows she's assessing him as prey. 'Something broken inside' sounds like she's identifying weakness, not investigating motives.

issues.line_text: Six months I'd been here. Six months preparing.
issues.description: 'Preparing' is investigator/planner language. What has she been preparing? Evidence collection, surveillance setup, investigation materials. A predator would say they've been 'waiting' not 'preparing.'
issues.fix: Six months I'd been here. Six months waiting for this.
issues.rationale: Predators wait for the right moment/opportunity. 'Waiting for this' sounds ominous (readers think: waiting to strike) without revealing the investigation/evidence-gathering activities implied by 'preparing.'

issues.description: Borderline acceptable but slightly clinical. 'In motion' is neutral planner language. Could be more viscerally predatory.
issues.rationale: 'Beginning' is simpler and more ominous. Less tactical/planner language, more inevitable-fate language that suits the predator framing.

notes: Most of the chapter is strong and maintains Eleanor's predatory framing well. The masturbation scene is excellent misdirectionΓÇöreaders will think obsession = dangerous predator, not grieving investigator. The 'watching' theme is well-executed. The main issues are scattered investigator-language patterns ('research,' 'preparation,' 'analyzing his facade') that need to shift toward predator-language ('waiting,' 'watching for weakness,' 'exploiting his trust').
